collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ROLE MODELS AND GOOD EXAMPLES, RM-41 to RM-90 (draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Fifty more events continuing your "Role Models and Good Examples — 40 Events". Same shape as yours: a SETUP, choices A-D (a few have three), and two possible outcomes per choice; the game picks one outcome from the chosen choice.

ledger.why: the owner (2026-11-15): the person the event is about is a cast villager shown by name, the role word kept as flavor (the villager need not have that job)

collection.description: A weaving teacher notices that one child keeps reaching for the fibers with the left hand.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (Name1), a weaving teacher, notices that one child keeps reaching for the fibers with the left hand, and the child's pattern keeps coming out backward.

choices.label: Ask Another Left-Handed Weaver to Help.
Let the Child Find Their Own Way.
Ask What Feels Natural to the Child.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: The teacher works facing the child, and the pattern finally makes sense.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: The mirrored lesson confuses the teacher more than the child, but they work it out together.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: An older left-handed weaver shows the child a few tricks nobody else knew.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: The older weaver learned the right-handed way long ago and is curious to try the other way too.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: The child invents a slightly different method that works perfectly well.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: The child's method is slow at first, but the teacher praises the steady progress.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: The child explains which steps feel awkward, and the teacher changes only those.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: The child does not know how to explain it, so they simply try several ways until one feels right.
